correctness.rationale: The rook graph is exactly the line graph of K_{m,n}. A selected edge uv has induced rook degree d_H(u)+d_H(v)-2, so the constraint is d_H(u)+d_H(v)≤4. If a vertex has degree three, all neighbors are leaves and the component is K_{1,3}; otherwise components are alternating paths, even cycles or isolates. The labelled two-sort exponential formula sums exact path, cycle, star contributions, including removal of the forbidden two-cycle. In a square, |E(H)|≤|V(H)|≤2q, with equality iff H is a spanning bipartite two-factor. For total domination when max(m,n)≥5, a chosen vertex has at least 5 rook neighbors, at most 2 chosen; a complement vertex with no complement neighbor would make four chosen vertices in a row/column clique, contradicting max degree two. Direct subset tests of boards up to 3×4 and exact 2×2,3×3 maxima corroborate but do not prove universal statements.

value.rationale: The exact three-independence polynomial is a natural coefficientwise graph invariant beyond known extremal k-independence numbers. The spanning two-factor extremizers give exact multiplicities, and a nontrivial large-board equivalence produces total outer three-independent domination polynomials; these are useful precise quantities and not an arbitrary parameter slice.

final_claim: For every m,n≥0 the induced maximum-degree-at-most-two polynomial of K_m square K_n has the stated alternating-path/even-cycle/three-star EGF; q×q maxima have cardinality 2q and count (q!)²[t^q] exp(-t/2)/sqrt(1-t), and for min(m,n)≥2,max(m,n)≥5 the complementary sets are totally dominating.
